overrides.tts_text: And Dhritarashtra hearing the ill news of the success of the Pandavas and recollecting the resolutions of Duryodhana, Karna, and Sakuni, pondered for a while and addressed to Sanjaya the following speech:

overrides.speaker: dhritarashtra
overrides.direction: an old blind king justifying himself to his minister; defensive, bitter, weary

overrides.speaker: dhritarashtra
overrides.direction: the litany begins: bitter wonder at each success of the Pandavas

overrides.speaker: dhritarashtra
overrides.direction: the litany through exile and war: hope draining away line by line; vary the weight, never sing-song

overrides.speaker: dhritarashtra
overrides.direction: broken, on the edge of fainting

overrides.contains: that Sakti was hurled against Ghatotkacha by Karna
overrides.tts_text: When I heard that in the encounter between Karna and Ghatotkacha, that Sakti was hurled against Ghatotkacha by Karna, the same which was certainly to have slain Arjuna in battle, then, O Sanjaya, I had no hope of success.

When I heard that Nakula, the son of Madri, having in the presence of the whole army engaged in single combat with the son of Drona and showing himself equal to him drove his chariot in circles around, then, O Sanjaya, I had no hope of success.

overrides.speaker: sanjaya
overrides.direction: a wise minister consoling a grieving king: steady, compassionate, unhurried

overrides.contains: it behoveth thee not to grieve
it behoveth thee not to throw away thy reason
overrides.direction: gentle, firm close of the consolation

overrides.contains: When I heard that Kama and Duryodhana resolved
overrides.tts_text: When I heard that Karna and Duryodhana resolved upon imprisoning Krishna displayed in himself the whole universe, then, O Sanjaya, I had no hope of success.
When Karna said unto Bhishma—I will not fight when thou art fighting—and, quitting the army, went away, then, O Sanjaya, I had no hope of success.

overrides.direction: the king's grief quieted; gentle resolution
